newsitem.title: USA: Lucent, Philips form $2.5 billion phone company.
newsitem.headline: Lucent, Philips form $2.5 billion phone company.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. and Philips Electronics NV of the Netherlands said Tuesday they will combine the biggest makers of consumer telephones and related products in the United States and Europe into a jointly owned company with annual sales of about $2.5 billion.

The company, to be called Philips Consumer Communications, will make corded and cordless phones and answering machines and develop and market digital and analogue cellular phones, pagers and other consumer products.

Philips will own 60 percent of the venture and Lucent the other 40 percent. The venture brings together the $1.4 billion consumer products business of Philips, Europe's biggest electronics company, and the $1.1 billion consumer telephone business at Lucent, the telephone equipment-making company that was spun off by AT&T Corp. last year.

Officials said the venture would allow the new company to sell new products in new markets. Philips is the leading maker of corded and cordless phones in Europe and Lucent is the biggest maker of phones and answering machines in the United States.

"The only overlap is upside," said Michael McTighe, managing director of Philips' existing consumer electronics arm and the chief executive of the new venture. He said, for example, that Lucent's phone products, currently sold mainly in the United States, could be targeted at markets overseas.

"There are many markets in Latin America and Asia where we can offer those products in a short period of time," he said, noting they meet Federal Communications Commission standards that exceed communications standards in most countries.
McTighe said the only major country where neither company has a major presence was Japan, but that the venture would be looking to break into that market in the coming year.
"Next year we will attack there," he said.
The venture will be based in Parsippany, N.J., near Lucent's Basking Ridge, N.J., headquarters, while a search for a permanent base takes place, officials said.
The executives said the new venture took shape quickly after talks began two to three months ago, which officials credited to the lack of overlap in the companies' operations.
The companies said they expect "the vast majority" of the 8,400 Lucent and the 4,000 Philips employees in their consumer telephone businesses to move to the new venture.
The ownership represents the approximate revenue contribution of the two companies, a Lucent spokeswoman said.

Carly Fiorina, a Lucent executive who had recently taken the helm of Lucent's consumer products business as president, noted that Lucent's domestic market share was double that of any rival in corded and cordless phones and answering machines.
She will serve on the board of the new venture.
Lucent's stock rose $2.25 to $70.125 and Philips U.S. shares jumped $3.625 to $66.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
